_README: Label id -> structure name for the upper-limb bone label volume produced from the Visible Human male frozen CT by scripts/segment_arm_bones_vhm.py (HU threshold, marker-controlled watershed on the smoothed CT; markers from the TotalSegmentator `total` humerus label and the densest forearm cortex), plus the reviewed mapping onto atlas entities.

A KEY, not data: it contains no anatomy and no geometry. The reconstruction field of view (480 mm) clips both arms around the elbow, so every bone here is PARTIAL: the humerus lacks its distal end, the radius and ulna lack their proximal ends (about 85% and 65% of their length is in the scan, along the bone axis), and the hand is complete but unseparated.
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), series 5d409385-d3e7-48a9-ae50-150b39e834da via the NCI Imaging Data Commons mirror (Fedorov A et al., Radiographics 2023, doi:10.1148/rg.230180). Segmentation produced in this repository; radius/ulna identity by distal width (radius wider) confirmed by distal reach (radial styloid lower), both sides.

humerus_right.note: TotalSegmentator humerus label extended distally by watershed; distal end truncated by the field of view.

radius_right.note: Proximal end truncated by the field of view (no radial head/neck).

ulna_right.note: Proximal end truncated by the field of view (no olecranon/coronoid).

hand_right.note: All hand bones in one mask; the atlas keeps carpals, metacarpals and phalanges as separate entities, so this maps to the composite hand_r.

humerus_left.note: TotalSegmentator humerus label extended distally by watershed; distal end truncated by the field of view.

radius_left.note: Proximal end truncated by the field of view (no radial head/neck).

ulna_left.note: Proximal end truncated by the field of view (no olecranon/coronoid).

hand_left.note: All hand bones in one mask; the atlas keeps carpals, metacarpals and phalanges as separate entities, so this maps to the composite hand_l.
